exercise.title: Why do distinct linear factors produce logarithms?

statement.p: Writing 1/((x-1)(x+2))=A/(x-1)+B/(x+2) turns the integral into two logarithms. In your own words, why is that split possible, and why does each simple linear denominator integrate to a logarithm?

hint.p: A linear denominator has a nonzero constant derivative. Substituting that linear expression as u turns its reciprocal into a constant multiple of 1/u, whose antiderivative is \ln|u|.

exercise.title: Why does a repeated factor need every power?

statement.p: For (x-r)^2 in the denominator, both A/(x-r) and B/(x-r)^2 appear. In your own words, why is one fraction not enough, and what contradiction appears if the highest power is missing?

hint.p: After clearing the denominator, a missing highest-power term can force 1=0 at the repeated root. Every power is needed to span the possible numerators.

subsection.p: Not every quadratic factors into real linear terms. For example,

exercise.title: Why does an irreducible quadratic need a linear numerator?

statement.p: Over x^2+1 we write (Bx+C)/(x^2+1), not a constant alone. In your own words, why is the Bx term needed, and how does it separate a logarithm coming from the derivative of the quadratic from an arctangent coming from the constant term?

hint.p: The derivative of x^2+1 is 2x, which produces \ln(x^2+1). What remains after that piece is peeled off is a constant over x^2+1, which is an arctangent.

subsection.p: The method is systematic.

We now have several strong methods: substitution, integration by parts, trigonometric identities, trigonometric substitution, and partial fractions. The difficult part is no longer only carrying out a method. It is choosing the method. That is the next question.

exercise.title: Why is partial fractions algebra before calculus?

statement.p: The method begins only after the rational function is proper, and it splits one complicated fraction into simpler pieces. In your own words, why must you divide first when the numerator’s degree is too large, and why is the integration step almost an afterthought?

hint.p: The pieces 1/(x-r) and (Ax+B)/(x^2+1) already have known antiderivatives. The work is rewriting the integrand so those pieces appear.
